executive_summary: Today's information landscape is defined by the critical thread of systemic realignment under pressure, stretching from geopolitical flashpoints to domestic governance. This theme connects the looming strategic crises detailed in Foreign Affairs—such as the escalating nuclear standoff in the Gulf and China's quiet expansion—with the sudden consolidation of political power in breaking news regarding Republican holdouts rallying behind Blanche's nomination. Just as military analysts and AI researchers study how systems adapt, lie, or break when pushed to their limits, policymakers and institutions are rapidly closing ranks to secure outcomes before deadlines hit. Ultimately, this convergence matters because it highlights a global pivot toward consolidation, where traditional norms are sidelined in favor of decisive power plays.

items.headline: Toasted Coconut Rice Salad
items.blurb: Kayla Hoang’s colorful and crunchy toasted coconut rice salad. The purple cabbage and cashews give it plenty of texture, while the coconut rice adds a gentle sweetness. Then, to finish it off with verve, Kayla tosses everything with a ginger dressing brightened with ponzu.

items.headline: Chickpeas al limone with burrata
items.blurb: Hetty Lui McKinnon’s braised chickpea recipe was inspired by the classic Italian dish spaghetti al limone. The soft clouds of burrata make this extra special, turning the sauce creamy and rich.

items.headline: Chile tofu
items.blurb: Another one from Hetty, her spicy vegan riff on chile paneer — the classic Indo-Chinese stir-fry from Kolkata, India — practically explodes with flavor. Coating the tofu in cornstarch before pan-frying it lends a lovely crispness and helps it stand up to the zippy, Sriracha-spiked sauce. Serve it with rice to mellow the heat.

items.headline: Creamy cottage cheese basil pasta
items.blurb: Ali Slagle’s one-pot pasta has the herby, garlic-forward flavors of pesto but is imbued with cottage cheese. The key to getting the right texture here is to use a high-speed blender or food processor and let the machine run until the sauce is silky-smooth. Then toss it with your favorite pasta for a summery, easy meal.

items.headline: Lemon chicken with asparagus
items.blurb: Peak asparagus season has come and gone, so feel free to make this flavorful sheet-pan meal with broccoli, bell peppers or green beans instead. Any of them will happily absorb the garlicky, citrusy flavors of the sauce.

items.headline: Peanut butter protein granola
items.blurb: I tend to agree with my friend Robin, who once said that granola was really just an excuse to eat oatmeal raisin cookies for breakfast. But by stirring peanut butter, hemp seeds and egg whites into the usual mix of oats, nuts and honey, Yossy Arefi adds enough protein to make her recipe a nutrient-rich way to start your day.

items.headline: UEFA threatens FIFA

items.headline: Polk retires
items.blurb: Ja’Lynn Polk, a second-round NFL Draft pick just two years ago, is heading to the reserve/retired list, per an announcement from the Saints, who traded for him last summer. New England selected Polk out of Washington in the 2024 draft, but the 24-year-old struggled to find his place in the Pats’ offense. Now he’s already out of the league.Read more on where things went wrong
